definitions: To continue to hold something or someone.
To wait, especially on the telephone.
To continue to do something or to keep something, often despite difficulties.
To maintain a belief or idea.
examples: She was holding on to the railing during the storm.
Please keep holding on, the next available agent will be with you shortly.
They are holding on to hope for a better future.
He's holding on to the idea that things will improve.
